title: Research Science Institute (RSI) 2027
org: Center for Excellence in Education · MIT / Stanford
description: A six-week, cost-free STEM research programme with coursework and mentored original research at MIT or Stanford.
eligibility: For high school juniors (typically Grade 11, about to enter their final year). Sophomores and seniors are not eligible. International applicants have a separate application route; review its specific rules.

title: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS) 2027
cost: Paid · need-based aid and fee waivers
description: A two-week residential academic programme at Yale with interdisciplinary sessions, seminars and a global student cohort.
eligibility: Applicants from all countries, including Pakistan, may apply. Must be 16–18 by July 18, 2027, currently a high school sophomore or junior (or equivalent), and meet the graduation-year and first-time-participant rules. Regular Decision application fee is US$100; eligible students may request a fee waiver. Need-based aid can cover up to 100% of tuition for selected students; travel support is limited.

title: NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026
description: A global 48-hour hackathon using NASA data to solve real-world challenges. Registration and project submission close during the event weekend.
eligibility: Participants can choose an in-person or virtual local event, including the Universal virtual event. Important for Lahore: its in-person event page says capacity has been reached; choose a virtual event instead. Check the official event page for team and submission rules.

title: IEOx Essay Challenge 2026/27
cost: Fee not stated · confirm with organiser
description: An international essay competition on climate economics, sustainable finance, carbon markets and environmental policy. Top 40 papers are shortlisted, with five special awards.
eligibility: Open to junior/middle and senior/secondary high school students worldwide who will be under 20 on June 30, 2027. Individual entries or teams of up to three. English; 250–400 word abstract and 1,500–2,000 word essay; APA citations. The rules prohibit unauthorised third-party generation.

title: Lumiere Scholars Essay Award · Fall 2026
deadlineText: Free registration Nov 30 · Essay Dec 20, 2026 · 11:59 PM EST
cost: Free to enter · prizes and scholarships
description: A global research-based argumentative essay award. Six winners share more than US$11,000 in cash awards and programme scholarships; selected students may be invited to an Oxford symposium and gala.
eligibility: Open worldwide to students enrolled in high school on Dec 31, 2026. One original, sole-authored English essay of up to 2,000 words, using MLA 8. Free registration closes Nov 30; final essay submission closes Dec 20 at 11:59 PM EST. Read the organiser’s academic-integrity rules before submitting.

title: International AI Startup Challenge 2026–27
deadlineText: Register by Dec 15 · Submit by Dec 20, 2026
cost: Free · no entry or submission fee
description: Build an AI-powered startup idea over a seven-week cycle, then submit a pitch and founder Q&A. Participants receive scored feedback; finalists pitch online.
eligibility: Open worldwide to students aged 13–18. Compete solo or in teams of up to five; no coding experience required. Under-18 participants must confirm parent or guardian permission at registration. Registration closes Dec 15; submissions close Dec 20. No cash prizes are offered in this inaugural cycle.

title: Zero Robotics 2027 High School Tournament
cost: Fee not stated · confirm with organiser
description: An international programming tournament where teams code Astrobee, the free-flying robot aboard the International Space Station, for a simulated mission.
eligibility: Open to high school students internationally. Teams must have at least four students. The programme runs Jan 11–Feb 12, 2027, with the final event planned for Feb 19. Check the official registration page for team, mentor and fee details.

title: WHN Student Internship 2026–2027
description: An 8–12 week remote internship running December 2026 to February 2027, contributing to public-health education, research summaries, webinars, podcasts or a children’s magazine.
eligibility: The organiser says high school and college students worldwide are welcome. Flexible scheduling; unpaid. Review the role details and any age or guardian-consent requirements on the official page before applying.

title: Remote Student Internship
deadlineText: No closing date listed · check application page
description: A flexible remote internship with Marketing & Communications, Partnerships & Operations, or Fundraising & Development tracks. Includes a short course, at least two projects and manager reviews.
eligibility: The foundation states that high school and college students can apply from anywhere. Unpaid. Application asks for a resume; no programme closing date is published on the page. Confirm age requirements and guardian involvement if applicable.

title: Cisco x MoFEPT · 9 Free AI & Cybersecurity Courses
org: Pakistan Ministry of Federal Education & Professional Training · Cisco Networking Academy
cost: Free · digital badge / certificate details vary
description: Nine self-paced courses covering generative AI, prompting, AI for work, modern AI foundations and cybersecurity. The campaign runs Oct 13–Dec 7, 2026.
eligibility: A Pakistan-focused public campaign. Beginner-friendly and self-paced; a free Cisco NetAcad account is required. The official campaign says successful completion may earn a shareable Cisco digital badge and/or certificate, depending on the course.

title: Digital Learning & Skills Enrichment Initiative (DLSEI 3.0) · Cohort 4
deadlineText: Cohort 4 registration open · deadline not stated
cost: Free course access for approved students
description: Eligible university students can access more than 15,000 Coursera courses, professional certificates, learning tracks and specialisations through HEC’s initiative.
eligibility: For students enrolled in public- or private-sector universities. Your university focal person must verify the application; after approval, wait for the Coursera invitation. This is not listed as a school/high-school programme.

title: SCP International High School Poetry Competition 2026
level: High school / elementary students or age 19 and under
description: An international poetry competition with a US$250 first prize and publication opportunities. Poems must use metre and may be up to 50 lines.
eligibility: Open to high school or elementary students, or anyone aged 19 or younger, from any country. Entry costs US$10 per poem. The organiser explicitly prohibits AI tools from writing the poem. Check payment and prize-transfer requirements for entrants outside the United States.
